SMTO-MEM-0018 — SMTO couldn't reach the model that makes text searchable

GUID: dae3cc00-e866-5d5f-9e29-507cfe88e09f
Slug: knowledge-embedding-provider-unavailable
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • Knowledge sends text to an embeddings service to make it searchable. That service didn't answer, or answered with an error, so this document or search couldn't be processed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing and expand Embeddings. If it says Not assigned, choose an instance and select Assign Embeddings. With no embeddings model assigned, Knowledge has nowhere to send text.
  2. If Embeddings uses a managed instance, open Inference and check that the instance is running and ready. A stopped or failed instance can't answer, and SMTO only falls back to the CPU when a fallback is set up.
  3. If Document settings use Remote text endpoint, check that Remote API base URL is correct and that service is online and reachable from the SMTO server. SMTO sends text to that address and needs a working reply.
  4. Select Retry failed jobs in Knowledge, or Manage › Reindex on the affected document. Once the service answers, the stopped indexing can run again.

What success looks like

  • Documents show Ready to search, and Test retrieval returns passages.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; the Server log shows the exact connection error. Don't delete documents or Memory; their search data can be rebuilt once the service answers.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Embedding encode failed with embedding_provider_unavailable: no Embeddings connection is assigned, the managed instance and its CPU fallback both failed to return embeddings, or the remote endpoint's /embeddings request failed or returned an unusable response.

What this means

  • The app could not obtain usable embeddings from the selected service. Its address, credentials or availability need checking. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported embedding_provider_unavailable. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The embedding connection test succeeds.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Check that Settings, Model routing, Embeddings is assigned and verified. For a managed instance, check its health and CPU fallback configuration on the Inference page; for provider=http, test the endpoint's /embeddings route with the configured model and key and confirm it returns one vector per input with the profile's dimensions, then read the Server log for the underlying request error. Then retry failed jobs.
  • Ask an administrator to test the configured embedding connection in model settings. Check its address, authentication and service status before retrying indexing.

Retry and execution caution

  • The embedding connection test succeeds.

How to verify the fix

  • The embedding connection test succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
